purpose: Select useful settings for a situated reading of the game, with the interview as available context. Do not optimize lexical diversity alone.
priority_order: Grounding: distinguish a defensible reading of the visible text from invented events, specific unsupported motives, production causes, or biographical facts.
Observation: prefer an implication, tension, or association rooted in a specific detail over a paraphrase or a generic conclusion about the whole game.
Novelty: assess the claim against both provided prior comments; a changed noun does not make the same claim new.
Clarity: concise, readable English, two sentences within 90 words, suitable for display.
Interview use: a precise supported connection can add value; mentioning Briggs or a theme is not valuable on its own, and absence is not an automatic failure.
limitations: Literary interpretation is not a fact-retrieval task. A cautious interpretation can be valid even when the game does not state it explicitly.
Lexical counters and embedding similarities are descriptive, not quality scores.
The screen is exploratory: four scenes and two seeds per condition. Finalists require a rolling sequence and later game events.
Assessment is by the coding assistant, not an independent human panel; the user should judge the retained examples in the installation.
